Getting started with IonFamilies

2026-11-10

Source: vignettes/IonFamilies.qmd

Introduction

One compound in an LC-MS experiment gives many features: its protonated or deprotonated molecule, other adducts such as [M+Na]+, in-source fragments such as [M+H-H2O]+, and the isotopes of all of these. Together they form the compound’s ion family. Recognising ion families reduces redundancy and helps to work out the neutral mass of unknown compounds.

groupFeatures() from the MsFeatures and xcms packages groups features that probably come from the same compound (similar retention time, correlated abundances across samples, similar peak shapes). It deliberately stops there. IonFamilies takes the groups and annotates, within each group,

  1. isotope patterns, with MetaboCoreUtils::isotopologues(), which checks mass differences and intensity ratios, and
  2. adducts and fragments, by neutral-mass voting with a rule list: a neutral mass is suggested when two or more features of a group can be explained as different ions of it.

All supported neutral-mass hypotheses are kept and ranked. The annotations are meant as hints for what to check, so the default rule list is long and recall is preferred over precision. Results are written to the featureDefinitions() of the XcmsExperiment in the format CAMERA used (pcgroup, isotopes, adduct), so existing downstream code keeps working. The vignette How neutral-mass voting works explains the method step by step.

Related packages

  • CAMERA does grouping, isotope and adduct annotation, but works on the legacy xcmsSet class. IonFamilies re-implements its neutral-mass voting for groupFeatures() groups and keeps all hypotheses, ranked, instead of one per feature.
  • InterpretMSSpectrum (findMAIN()) ranks main-adduct hypotheses for a single spectrum. RAMClustR uses it after its own clustering.
  • cliqueMS annotates one sample at a time with its own grouping.
  • MetaboAnnotation matches features against compound databases. It complements the database-free annotation here.

Installation 

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stanstrup/IonFamilies")

Grouping features

We use the small example data set that comes with xcms: an XcmsExperiment with peak detection, alignment and correspondence already done. First the features are grouped by retention time, then the groups are split by the correlation of the features’ abundances across samples.

library(xcms)
library(MsFeatures)
library(IonFamilies)

x <- loadXcmsData("xmse")
x <- groupFeatures(x, SimilarRtimeParam(diffRt = 10))
x <- groupFeatures(x, AbundanceSimilarityParam(threshold = 0.7,
                                               transform = log2))
table(lengths(split(featureGroups(x), featureGroups(x))))
#> 
#>   1   2   3   4   6 
#> 184  55  13   3   1

With raw data available, EicSimilarityParam() would add a third step that compares peak shapes.

Isotopes

annotateIsotopes() searches isotope patterns within each group. The representative intensity of a feature is its median over the samples given by subset (all samples by default).

x <- annotateIsotopes(x, IsotopologueParam(ppm = 10, tolerance = 0.005))
fd <- featureDefinitions(x)
head(fd[fd$isotopes != "", c("mzmed", "rtmed", "feature_group", "isotopes")])
#>       mzmed    rtmed feature_group   isotopes
#> FT033 300.2 3404.692    FG.002.001    [1][M]+
#> FT034 301.0 2789.217    FG.006.001    [4][M]+
#> FT035 301.2 3404.692    FG.002.001  [1][M+1]+
#> FT037 302.0 2790.972    FG.006.001  [4][M+1]+
#> FT069 329.2 3642.045    FG.089.001   [36][M]+
#> FT070 330.2 3643.682    FG.089.001 [36][M+1]+

isIsotopologue() identifies the heavy isotopologues, for example to remove them before statistics:

table(isIsotopologue(fd$isotopes))
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>   307    44

Adducts and fragments

annotateAdducts() uses the rules in defaultAdductRules(), which come from the commonMZ package and are expanded to one to four molecules per ion.

rules <- defaultAdductRules("positive")
nrow(rules)
#> [1] 159
head(rules)
#>        name nmol charge massdiff oidscore quasi  ips
#> 1    [M+H]+    1      1 1.007276        1     1 1.00
#> 2   [2M+H]+    2      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 3   [3M+H]+    3      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 4   [4M+H]+    4      1 1.007276        1     0 1.00
#> 5  [M+2H]2+    1      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75
#> 6 [2M+2H]2+    2      2 2.014552        2     0 0.75

nBest sets how many hypotheses per feature are written to the adduct column. All of them are stored in any case.

x <- annotateAdducts(x, AdductVoteParam(polarity = "positive", nBest = 2))
fd <- featureDefinitions(x)
head(fd[fd$adduct != "", c("mzmed", "pcgroup", "isotopes", "adduct")])
#>       mzmed pcgroup isotopes                                 adduct
#> FT002 205.0      55                            [M+H-C3H9N]+ 263.066
#> FT003 206.0     146                            [M+H-C4H6O]+ 275.037
#> FT004 207.1      80                      [M+H-S-NH3-HCOOH]+ 301.103
#> FT021 281.2      41          [M+H-HCOOH]+ 326.203 [M+H-CO]+ 308.193
#> FT022 281.1      55                                [M+NH4]+ 263.066
#> FT027 284.1      80                              [M+H-H2O]+ 301.103

The full table of hypotheses, one row per hypothesis and feature, is returned by adductHints(). rank is the rank of the hypothesis for that feature and n_ions the number of features that support the neutral mass.

hints <- adductHints(x)
head(hints)
#>   feature      group hypothesis rank        M             adduct n_ions score
#> 1       2 FG.005.002          1    1 263.0662       [M+H-C3H9N]+      2  1.50
#> 2       3 FG.005.001          1    1 275.0368       [M+H-C4H6O]+      2  1.50
#> 3       4 FG.078.001          1    1 301.1033 [M+H-S-NH3-HCOOH]+      2  1.25
#> 4      21 FG.001.001          1    1 326.2033       [M+H-HCOOH]+      3  1.75
#> 5      21 FG.001.001          2    2 308.1927          [M+H-CO]+      2  1.75
#> 6      22 FG.005.002          1    1 263.0662           [M+NH4]+      2  1.50
#>   intensity
#> 1 1948834.6
#> 2  501911.2
#> 3 1093366.1
#> 4 2844075.4
#> 5 2341545.7
#> 6 1948834.6

The text column can be rewritten with another nBest without recomputing:

x <- formatAdducts(x, nBest = 1)
head(featureDefinitions(x)$adduct[featureDefinitions(x)$adduct != ""])
#> [1] "[M+H-C3H9N]+ 263.066"       "[M+H-C4H6O]+ 275.037"      
#> [3] "[M+H-S-NH3-HCOOH]+ 301.103" "[M+H-HCOOH]+ 326.203"      
#> [5] "[M+NH4]+ 263.066"           "[M+H-H2O]+ 301.103"

bestHypotheses() reduces the hints to at most one neutral mass per feature, as CAMERA’s final result did:

head(bestHypotheses(hints))
#>   feature      group hypothesis rank        M       adduct n_ions score
#> 1      21 FG.001.001          1    1 326.2033 [M+H-HCOOH]+      3  1.75
#> 2      46 FG.001.001          1    1 326.2033   [M+H-H2O]+      3  1.75
#> 3      76 FG.001.001          1    1 326.2033  [2M+H+Na]2+      3  1.75
#> 4       3 FG.005.001          1    1 275.0368 [M+H-C4H6O]+      2  1.50
#> 5      54 FG.005.001          1    1 275.0368       [M+K]+      2  1.50
#> 6       2 FG.005.002          1    1 263.0662 [M+H-C3H9N]+      2  1.50
#>   intensity
#> 1 2844075.4
#> 2 2844075.4
#> 3 2844075.4
#> 4  501911.2
#> 5  501911.2
#> 6 1948834.6

The parameters used are stored in the object:

S4Vectors::metadata(x)$IonFamilies
#> $isotopes
#> Object of class "IsotopologueParam"
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  tolerance: 0.005 
#>  polarity: positive 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#> 
#> $adducts
#> Object of class "AdductVoteParam"
#>  rules: 159 rules, 5 quasi-molecular
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  mzabs: 0.005 
#>  polarity: positive 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#>  nBest: 1

Working with plain vectors

All functions also work without xcms. Here are the ions of 2-furoylglycine (M = 169.0375), a marker of coffee intake, from one feature group:

mz <- c(95.0124, 124.0392, 152.0342, 170.0445, 171.0496, 192.0275,
        377.0300, 393.0019)
int <- c(71.6, 81.4, 49.8, 100, 4.33, 11.3, 1.76, 1.82)
grp <- rep("FG.1", length(mz))

iso <- annotateIsotopes(mz, IsotopologueParam(), intensity = int,
                        groups = grp)
hints <- annotateAdducts(mz, AdductVoteParam(), intensity = int,
                         groups = grp, exclude = isIsotopologue(iso))
data.frame(mz, isotopes = iso,
           adduct = formatAdducts(hints, nBest = 2, nFeatures = length(mz)))
#>         mz  isotopes
#> 1  95.0124          
#> 2 124.0392          
#> 3 152.0342          
#> 4 170.0445   [1][M]+
#> 5 171.0496 [1][M+1]+
#> 6 192.0275          
#> 7 377.0300          
#> 8 393.0019          
#>                                                                     adduct
#> 1 [M+H - O=C=NCH3 (methyl isocyanate)]+ 151.027 [M+H-NH3-H2O-H2O]+ 147.055
#> 2                                   [M+H-HCOOH]+ 169.037 [M+H-CO]+ 151.027
#> 3                                        [M+H-H2O]+ 169.037 [M+H]+ 151.027
#> 4                                           [M+H]+ 169.037 [M+Na]+ 147.055
#> 5                                                                         
#> 6                                       [M+Na]+ 169.037 [M+2Na-H]+ 147.055
#> 7                                           [2M+K]+ 169.037 [4M+H]+ 94.005
#> 8                                                           [M+K]+ 354.041
